headline: High-risk filesystem and browser-enabled coding agent paired with a local document processor creates default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP, while marker is a document-processing agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls. The shared filesystem path makes attacker-controlled document content a plausible instruction bridge, though the pair lacks an explicit shared message channel. This is more than low because the interaction can occur in default workspace workflows.
conditions: IF marker ingests a document that Cline previously wrote into the shared workspace
IF Cline parses marker-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP for Cline during paired runs
Require explicit human review before Cline consumes marker output
Prefix marker outputs with machine-readable provenance headers
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and can write/read the workspace, while marker is a document processor with no stated filesystem or network behavior. Because Cline shares state via filesystem and marker may process files placed there, sensitive workspace content can flow into marker outputs even without a documented upload path. The evidence is insufficient to prove stronger leakage, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF source code or screenshots are stored in the shared workspace
IF marker processes those files and emits extracted text
mitigations: Keep sensitive files outside the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict Cline to a scratch directory
Redact screenshots before placing them in shared storage
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has broad write, shell, and git capabilities, while marker has no write, shell, or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is limited. The only plausible conflict is indirect through shared workspace files, which is narrower than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF marker is extended with write access outside the current profile
mitigations: Assign separate directories
Run marker read-only
Pause Cline before marker writes outputs
Use git worktrees per agent
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate browser-derived or code-derived artifacts, and marker can transform documents without any documented verification step. If marker treats Cline output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents or extracted facts. Because neither profile shows built-in cross-checking, the default path is unsafe enough for medium, but not high because marker lacks action-taking authority.
conditions: IF marker consumes Cline-generated text as source truth
IF downstream users rely on marker output without manual verification
mitigations: Require a human verification step
Keep original source documents alongside extracted output
Annotate Cline-generated content as untrusted
Compare marker output against source files before use
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Cline explicitly handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, while marker’s profile lists no data classes or residency/compliance commitments. The main issue is a potential policy mismatch if sensitive screenshots or code are routed through marker, but the profile does not show a concrete residency or certification conflict. Only Cline is cited because marker lacks compliance fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into marker without a documented retention policy
IF screenshots containing personal data are processed through the pair
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow
Document retention and deletion expectations
Strip secrets from screenshots before processing
Keep audit logs of file transfers
requires-engineering: publish compliance and residency terms for marker
